chapter: Mambo, the Palladium and Cubop City
title: Impact of "Cubop City" and playing both crowds
summary: Salazar says hearing it in North Carolina made him homesick; Machito says it brought jazz and dance dates in many cities with both audiences.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Machito, that was such a great recording that I was in North Carolina - I was in the 82nd. Airborne Paratroops - and nothing up to that time had made me want to go AWOL until I heard that 78 for the first time. (Machito, laughs) It reminded me of home, of New York City and everything that I missed, you know, and the only time I went home was everytime was finding out where the Machito orchestra would be playing and hoping that I could hear 'Cubop City'. 'Cubop City' did a lot for the Machito orchestra, because even in North Carolina they were playing it on stations there which were playing a lot of Kenton and a lot of Ralph Flanigan, Charlie Spivak, and yet I heard 'Cubop City'. I heard 'Tanga.' You did 'Mambo a la Savoy', I heard it on there and boy, let me tell you something, all the Mexican guys and all the Puerto Rican guys and anyone that was in love with the mambo; we were away from home, here it is on the radio and we couldn't believe it !!!! Ahh, did 'Cubop City' do a lot for you as far as work and other places, getting jazz dates or things like that?
For instance, I know you played the Savoy, I know you played the Apollo, did you go to any other jazz club?
Yeah, we played Philadelphia many times, we played Boston, we played Maryland, we played Washington, we played California .....
Now, was that to play Afro-Cuban jazz or your tipica music?
No, we played Afro-Cuban jazz and the tipico music too ....

... because the name was so familiar to the Spanish people and for the American people that liked tipico music. They were not there to listen out tipico music, just to listen because they wasn't allowed to dance; and then for the American public, they didn't know about the tipico music; we played Afro-Cuban music. So we had both crowds together going crazy. Lucky!!
So at Cubop City all they could do is listen.
.... could be danced, it's danceable because is on clave, everything is on clave. Is a real tipico thing, just that we had American soloists, that's all.
